Kalvarija New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marijampolės apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the newer of Kalvarija's Jewish cemeteries. The town, founded in the 17th century, may have been preceded by a group of Jewish weavers in the village of Trabi; a royal decree permitted a synagogue's construction in 1713, replaced by a stone building in 1803. The population reached 3,072 (56 percent) by 1827, with close ties to Königsberg and strong influence from the German Haskalah; the 1880s saw significant emigration to the US, South Africa, and Palestine. By 1923, 1,233 Jews remained, and in 1939 the community sheltered about 800 Jewish refugees fleeing the German-occupied Suwałki area. Following the 1941 German invasion, Jews were seized for forced labor and transferred to Marijampolė, documented elsewhere in this collection, where they were murdered; local Lithuanians, led by a priest, then demolished Jewish shops and used the bricks to build a new church fence.
